column4: The source-section root غ ش و names a coming-over that covers: here the sea overwhelms Pharaoh's pursuing army (فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ الْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ), a concrete destructive arrival.
The source-section root غ ش و appears as the overturned townships are covered by what covered them (فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ); the word's covering sense is staged as punishment.
The source-section root غ ش و covers the faces of wrongdoers with pieces of dark night (أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ); it carries the covering image into the contrary face-state of judgment.
Night covers the day and pursues it rapidly; this is a recurring, ordinary covering that gives a concrete secondary sense to the source-section's Ghashiya image.
The same night-covering of day recurs here; its ordinary cycle contrasts with the overwhelming cover of the source image.

The source-section's root و ل ي with عن means turning away and leaving nearness; this verse asks what turned people away from their qibla (مَا وَلَّاهُمْ عَن قِبْلَتِهِمْ), an especially close parallel.
The qibla passage says some will turn back on their heels (يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ); the ayah's own contribution is the reversal from following the Messenger when tested.
On the Day faces become white or black (تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ), a direct two-sided face scene parallel to al-Ghashiya's divided groups.
The next ayah says the white-faced group is in God's mercy; it completes the favorable side introduced in 3:106.
On Resurrection Day, faces are blackened for those who lied about God (تَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهُهُم); it links denial to the adverse face-state.
The next ayah says God saves those who were mindful; it supplies the favorable counterpart to 39:60's blackened faces.
Each person's record is attached to them and brought forth as an open book on Resurrection Day; this begins a concrete account scene after the source's return.
The person is told to read the book, with oneself sufficient as reckoner (حَسِيبًا); the source-section's root ح س ب is directly present.
On that Day a person is informed of what they sent ahead and left behind; this continues the settled destination in 75:12 with the disclosure/account that follows return.
The next ayah says a person is a witness against themself, making the account self-evident after 75:13.
Even if a person offers excuses, the account stands; this completes 75:14's self-witness scene.
People are exposed on that Day and nothing hidden remains; this reverses the covering named by the source-section's root غ ش و.
The favorable person receives their record in the right hand; this begins the two-sided account scene after 69:18's exposure.
The favorable person says they expected to meet their account (إِنِّي ظَنَنتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ); the source-section's root ح س ب is explicit.
The other person is given the record in the left hand, contrasting with the favorable record in 69:19.
The person says they did not know what their account was (وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ); this continues the adverse reckoning with the source-section root ح س ب.
People are gathered for a Day of no doubt and each soul is fully paid for what it earned; it directly parallels return followed by account.
Believers give while fearing because they are returning to their Lord (أَنَّهُم إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ رَاجِعُونَ); return here produces humility rather than turning away.
All in the heavens and earth submit to God willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they return; it states both chosen and unavoidable return in one ayah.
God guides those who turn back to Him (مَن أَنَابَ إِلَيْهِ), a specific voluntary return matching the source-section's awāb branch.
Those who avoid false gods and turn back to God (أَنَابُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ) receive good news; the ayah gives a concrete favorable voluntary return.
The defiant are repeatedly sent back into the Fire when they try to leave it (أُعِيدُوا فِيهَا); this is a forced return to punishment beside the chosen return of 78:39.
When called to God and the Messenger for judgment, a party turns away (مُّعْرِضُونَ); the ayah places refusal in a specific judgment scene.
The next ayah contrasts that refusal: believers answer that they hear and obey when called to judgment, showing the positive response after 24:48.
A party given scripture turns away (يَتَوَلَّىٰ) when called to God's Book for judgment; the ayah joins turning away to refusal of an arriving decision.
Whoever turns away from the remembrance (يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ) is assigned a satanic companion; it gives a specific consequence for turning away from remembrance.
Whoever turns away from the reminder (أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ) will bear a burden on Resurrection Day, directly joining refusal to later judgment.
That burden remains with them on the Day of Resurrection; this completes 20:100's consequence for turning away.
Hell's keepers ask whether a warner came; this sets up the warning-and-response scene that parallels the image's arriving report.
The people admit a warner came but they denied him; this row's own contribution is the arrival of warning followed by rejection.
They say that if they had listened or reasoned, they would not be among the Fire's inhabitants; this gives their turning away its stated cause.
They confess their sin and are far from salvation; this completes the rejected-warning sequence with accountability.
Those who fear their Lord unseen receive forgiveness and great reward, the favorable counterpart to the rejecters in 67:9-11.
The trumpet is blown, the dead fall, then it is blown again and they stand looking; this gives a concrete arrival and rising before the account.
The earth shines, the record is placed, and prophets and witnesses are brought; this is the next stage of the accounting scene after 39:68.
Every soul is fully repaid for what it did; this completes 39:69's record-and-witness scene.
The greatest catastrophe comes (فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَىٰ), another arrival-form for the overwhelming Day.
On that Day a person remembers what they strove for; it supplies the response to the catastrophe arriving in 79:34.
The Fire is exposed for those who see; this completes the arrival scene with the adverse outcome.
People see the Day as far away (إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا), contrasting their distance from the punishment with the source's nearer opportunity to return.
God sees the same Day as near (وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا); this completes the contrast in 70:6.
Disbelievers claim the Hour will not come (لَا تَأْتِينَا السَّاعَةُ), directly opposing the source-section's root ء ت ي and its certainty of arrival.
The trumpet is blown and the threatened Day arrives; this is the immediate setup for the arriving soul and lifted cover in 50:21-22.
Each soul then knows what it sent ahead and left behind; this gives the reckoning after resurrection a specific act of disclosure.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it; this is a precise favorable result of the account after return.
Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it; it supplies the adverse counterpart to 99:7.
